planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant outdoors once danger of frost has passed.

directions: Yellow Pop is a bright-yellow snacking pepper bred for eating fresh off the plant, with very few seeds and maximum sweetness. Plants are compact and container-friendly, producing handfuls of crunchy, bite-sized fruit through the season. Start seed indoors and transplant after frost danger has passed for a long, productive harvest.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant outdoors once danger of frost has passed.

directions: Red Pop delivers maximum crunch and refreshingly light sweetness with minimal seeds, bred for popping straight from the plant into your mouth. The compact habit is designed for easy growing in small spaces, including patios and balconies. Start indoors and move outside after frost for a steady supply of super-sweet snacking peppers.

planting.note: Direct sow outdoors once soil has warmed and frost danger has passed; pumpkins resent root disturbance from transplanting.

directions: Snowman Mix produces white pumpkins in three different sizes that all mature around the same time, making them easy to stack into creative fall displays. The sprawling vines need ample garden room but reward growers with a coordinated harvest of small, medium, and large ghostly-white fruit. Direct sow after the soil has warmed for best results.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; nasturtiums dislike root disturbance and perform best when not transplanted.

directions: Sweethearts Mix offers a pastel blend of lemon, rose, and apricot-colored flowers held above lily-pad-shaped foliage for a soft, painterly display. The blooms and leaves are edible, adding peppery color to salads and garnishes. Direct sow after frost in average, well-drained soil; overly rich soil favors foliage over flowers.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost for a cool-season cutting-garden crop; grows best in cool weather and bolts or declines in summer heat.

directions: Iron Apricot pairs sturdy stems with soft apricot blooms and a rare, clove-like fragrance, making it a standout for cutting gardens and bouquets. Seedlings with round, dark-green cotyledons can be selected and kept to favor double flowers. Grow as a cool-season crop for summer and fall cut-flower harvests.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost for a cool-season cutting-garden crop.

directions: Iron White produces stunning white blooms with an intoxicating clove-like fragrance that lends luxury to any bouquet. For maximum double flowers, select and keep seedlings with round, dark-green cotyledons, thinning out the rest. A fragrant, cool-season stock for the cutting garden.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost for a cool-season cutting-garden crop.

directions: Iron Yellow combines strong, upright stems with yellow blooms and a sophisticated clove-like fragrance, making it a standout in cool-season cutting gardens. Its sturdy habit holds up well in arrangements and bouquets. Grow as a cool-season annual, sown indoors ahead of the last frost.

planting.note: Set out started plants after danger of frost has passed; sold as a 9-plant pack with three plants each of red, white, and blue.

directions: Old Glory Mix is a patriotic Easy Wave-type petunia blend combining red, white, and blue flowers, bred for America's 250th-anniversary celebrations. Plants cascade beautifully from hanging baskets, window boxes, and garden beds. Set out established plants after frost for season-long color.

planting.note: Set out started plants after last frost for summer bloom; sold as established plants rather than seed.

directions: Lavender Lisianthus produces doubled, rose-like flowers in a whisper-soft lavender shade that create billowing clouds of color in beds and borders. The long-lasting blooms also make luxuriant indoor bouquets. Set out transplants after frost in full sun for summer flowering.

planting.note: Set out started plants after last frost for summer bloom; sold as established plants rather than seed.

directions: First Love bears sweetly ruffled, double, rose-like flowers that are snow white with a soft dusting of pink, held on thornless stems. The blooms work equally well as a garden display plant or as a long-lasting cut flower. Set out transplants after frost in full sun for summer bloom.
